url: 'https://burger-api.com/docs/'

# Welcome to BurgerAPI

BurgerAPI is a Bun-first framework for building APIs. You create folders and files, and BurgerAPI turns them into routes. It works with TypeScript and JavaScript.

:::info A new BurgerAPI
`burger-api` and `@burger-api/cli` 1.0.0-beta are rebuilt from the ground up and install by default. Please try them and [open an issue](https://github.com/isfhan/burger-api/issues) if anything breaks or feels wrong. See the [release notes](https://burger-api.com/blog/burger-api-v1.0.0-beta-release) for what is new. Coming from `burger-api@0.9.7` or `@burger-api/cli@0.9.9`? The [migration guide](https://burger-api.com/docs/migration) covers every breaking change.
:::

### What you get

- **File-based routing:** a folder with a `route.ts` file is a route.
- **Validation:** define schemas in `schema.ts` and read typed data from `ctx.validated`.
- **Hooks:** run code at each step of a request, for example to log or check auth.
- **Plugins and providers:** add features in `src/plugins.ts` and shared services in `src/providers.ts`.
- **OpenAPI:** API docs generated from your routes, served at `/docs`.
- **WebSocket:** real-time routes under `src/websocket/`.
- **Deploy anywhere:** `burger-api build --target=bun|node|cloudflare|deno|vercel`.

# Quick Start

Get a BurgerAPI app running in under a minute.

## Prerequisites

- **[Bun](https://bun.sh/)**: the CLI and the dev server run on Bun, wherever you deploy later.

## Steps

1. **Install the CLI:**

    ```bash
    bun add -g @burger-api/cli
    ```

    You can also skip the install and run `bunx @burger-api/cli <command>`.

    If you see `burger-api: command not found`, add `~/.bun/bin` to your `PATH` (`%USERPROFILE%\.bun\bin` on Windows) and open a new terminal.

2. **Create a project and start the dev server:**

    ```bash
    burger-api create my-api
    cd my-api
    bun run dev
    ```

3. **Open** [http://localhost:4000/api](http://localhost:4000/api) for the starter route and [http://localhost:4000/docs](http://localhost:4000/docs) for the API docs.

## JavaScript

The project uses TypeScript by default. For JavaScript, pass `--lang js`:

```bash
burger-api create my-api --lang js
```

See [JavaScript](https://burger-api.com/docs/javascript).

## Deploy anywhere

When you are ready to ship, build for your platform: `bun` (default), `node`, `cloudflare`, `deno`, or `vercel`.

```bash
burger-api build src/index.ts --target=cloudflare
```

See [Deployment](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/bun) for each target and [Compatibility](https://burger-api.com/docs/compatibility) for what works where.

## Next steps

- [Installation](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/installation): other install options.
- [CLI Tool](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/cli): all CLI commands.
- [Key Concepts](https://burger-api.com/docs/key-concepts): routing, hooks, plugins, validation.
- [JavaScript](https://burger-api.com/docs/javascript): JavaScript with JSDoc types.
- [Deployment](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/bun): Bun, Node.js, Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Vercel.

# Installation

BurgerAPI runs on [Bun](https://bun.sh/). Install Bun 1.4.4 or newer first ([guide](https://bun.sh/docs/installation)), then check it:

```bash
bun --version
```

## Install the CLI

The `burger-api` CLI creates projects and adds hooks and plugins. Pick one way to install it:

- **With Bun** (recommended):

  ```bash
  bun add -g @burger-api/cli
  ```

  If you then see `burger-api: command not found`, add `~/.bun/bin` to your `PATH` (`%USERPROFILE%\.bun\bin` on Windows) and open a new terminal.

- **With the install script**, which installs a standalone executable:

  ```bash
  # macOS, Linux, WSL
  curl -fsSL https://burger-api.com/install.sh | bash
  ```

  ```powershell
  # Windows PowerShell
  irm https://burger-api.com/install.ps1 | iex
  ```

- **From [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/isfhan/burger-api/releases/latest)**: download the executable for your system and put it on your `PATH`. On Linux and macOS, run `chmod +x burger-api`.

You can also run it once without installing: `bunx @burger-api/cli create my-api`.

## Create and run a project

```bash
burger-api create my-api
cd my-api
bun run dev
```

See the [CLI Tool](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/cli) guide for every command.

## Update

:::tip Getting an error?
Update the CLI and the framework first. Most problems are already fixed there.
:::

```bash
bun add -g @burger-api/cli@latest   # the CLI (or run the install script again)
bun add burger-api@latest           # the framework, in your project
burger-api doctor                   # finds hooks and plugins to refresh
```

Hooks and plugins you added with `burger-api add` are copies in your project, so these updates do not change them. `burger-api doctor` tells you which ones are out of date and prints the command to refresh each one. See [Add Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/add#updating-a-copy).

Run `burger-api --version` to see which version you have. If it still shows an old version, another `burger-api` comes first on your `PATH`: remove it, or run the install script, which tells you where it is.

## Without the CLI

You can also set up a project by hand:

1. Create a Bun project and install BurgerAPI and Zod:

   ```bash
   bun init
   bun add burger-api zod
   ```

2. Create your entry file:

   ```typescript title="src/index.ts"
   import { Burger } from "burger-api";

   const app = new Burger({
     apiDir: "./src/api",
   });

   const port = Number(process.env.PORT) || 4000;
   app.serve(port, () => {
     console.log(`Server running on http://localhost:${port}`);
   });
   ```

3. Create your first route. Validation goes in the route's `schema.ts`:

   ```typescript title="src/api/schema.ts"
   import { z } from "zod";
   import type { MethodSchema } from "burger-api";

   export const GET = {
     query: z.object({ name: z.string().default("world") }),
   } satisfies MethodSchema;
   ```

   ```typescript title="src/api/route.ts"
   import { defineRoute } from "burger-api";
   import { GET as GetSchema } from "./schema";

   export const GET = defineRoute(GetSchema, (ctx) => {
     return Response.json({ message: `Hello, ${ctx.validated.query.name}!` });
   });
   ```

4. Run it:

   ```bash
   bun run src/index.ts
   ```

   Open `http://localhost:4000/api` (try `?name=Burger`) and `http://localhost:4000/docs`.

Next, see [Configuration](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/configuration) to learn how to set up your app.

- [Key Concepts](https://burger-api.com/docs/key-concepts)
- [Burger API CLI Tool](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/cli)

# Burger API CLI Tool

The `burger-api` CLI creates projects, adds hooks and plugins, runs your app while you develop, and builds it for production. Install it as described in [Installation](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/installation).

## Quick start

```bash
burger-api create my-api
cd my-api
bun run dev
```

Open `http://localhost:4000/api` and `http://localhost:4000/docs`. See [Quick Start](https://burger-api.com/docs/quick-start) for the full walkthrough.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| [`create <name>`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/create) | Creates a new project. |
| [`dev`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/dev) | Runs your app and restarts it when you save a file. |
| [`build`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/build) | Builds your app for Bun, Node, Cloudflare Workers, Deno or Vercel. |
| `start` | Runs the Bun build from `burger-api build`. |
| [`build:exec`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/build-exec) | Builds a single executable that runs without Bun installed. |
| [`list`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/list) | Shows the official hooks and plugins. |
| [`add <name...>`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/add) | Copies official hooks and plugins into your project. |
| [`generate <type> <name>`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/generate) | Creates a route, WebSocket route, hook or plugin from a template. |
| [`inspect`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/inspect) | Shows the routes, hooks and plugins the CLI finds in your project. |
| [`doctor`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/doctor) | Checks your project for problems. |
| [`skills`](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/skills) | Installs AI agent skills into your project. |

Run `burger-api <command> --help` to see every option.

### `start`

`burger-api start` runs `.build/bundle/app.js`, the output of `burger-api build` for Bun. If you change your code after building, `start` warns that the build is out of date: run `burger-api build` again. For other targets, run the build with the platform's own tool. See [Deployment](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/bun).

```bash
burger-api build
burger-api start
```

Options:

- `-p, --port <port>`: the port (default `$PORT`, else `4000`).
- `-f, --file <file>`: the file to run (default `.build/bundle/app.js`, else `src/index.ts`).

## Common workflows

**Create and run a project**

```bash
burger-api create my-api
cd my-api
bun run dev
```

**Add hooks and plugins**

```bash
burger-api list
burger-api add cors logger
```

The CLI prints where to register each one: hooks in `src/hooks.ts`, plugins in `src/plugins.ts`.

**Build for production**

```bash
burger-api build                  # Bun (default)
burger-api build --target=node    # Node: run "bun add @burger-api/node-server" first
burger-api build --target=cloudflare
```

## Project structure

`burger-api create` generates:

```text
my-api/
├── src/
│   ├── index.ts           # App entry
│   ├── hooks.ts           # Global hooks
│   ├── plugins.ts         # Plugins
│   ├── providers.ts       # Shared services
│   ├── openapi.config.ts  # OpenAPI and docs page settings
│   ├── types.ts           # App-wide types (TypeScript projects)
│   └── api/               # API routes
├── AGENTS.md              # Project rules for AI agents
├── burger.build.ts        # Build settings
├── package.json
└── tsconfig.json          # jsconfig.json in a JavaScript project
```

`burger-api add` creates `ecosystem/` for the hooks and plugins it copies.

## Environment variables

- `GITHUB_TOKEN`: used when the CLI downloads hooks, plugins and skills from GitHub. Set it if you hit GitHub's rate limit.
- `BURGER_API_LOCAL`: set to `1` to turn on [local mode](#local-mode).

## Troubleshooting

- **`burger-api: command not found`**: the folder with the `burger-api` executable is not on your `PATH`. Restart your terminal after installing. See [Installation](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/installation).
- **`Directory already exists`**: `create` needs a folder name that does not exist yet.
- **Could not fetch the hooks and plugins list**: the CLI could not reach GitHub. Check your connection.
- **Entry file not found**: run the command from your project root, or pass the entry with `-f`.

## Local mode

For working on BurgerAPI itself: `--local` (or `BURGER_API_LOCAL=1`) makes the CLI use your local checkout instead of npm and GitHub. See `LOCAL_TESTING.md` in the [burger-api repository](https://github.com/isfhan/burger-api).

## Related

- [Quick Start](https://burger-api.com/docs/quick-start)
- [Key Concepts](https://burger-api.com/docs/key-concepts)
- [Installation](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/installation)

# Key Concepts

These are the main ideas in BurgerAPI. Each section links to a page with more detail.

## File-based routing

Your folders are your URLs. A folder under `src/api/` with a `route.ts` file is a route. Next to it you can add `schema.ts`, `hooks.ts`, `openapi.ts`, and `config.ts`. Each route folder stands on its own: child folders do not inherit these files.

See [File-Based Routing](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/file-based-routing).

## Burger instance

`src/index.ts` creates one `Burger` instance and starts the server. Build settings live in `burger.build.ts` and are read by the CLI.

See [Burger Class](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/burger-class) and [Configuration](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/configuration).

## Context

Every handler gets one object, `ctx` (type `BurgerContext`). It holds the request, `ctx.params`, `ctx.query`, validated data in `ctx.validated`, and your services in `ctx.services`. Handlers return a standard `Response`.

```ts
import type { BurgerContext } from "burger-api";

export async function GET(ctx: BurgerContext) {
    return Response.json({ id: ctx.params.id });
}
```

See [Request Context](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/request-handling).

## Validation

Define a schema per method in `schema.ts`. BurgerAPI checks the request before your handler runs. Bad input gets a `422` error. Wrap the handler in `defineRoute(schema, handler)` to get `ctx.validated` typed for you.

See [Zod Validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/zod) and [Type Safety](https://burger-api.com/docs/advanced/type-safety).

## Hooks and plugins

- **Hooks** run at steps of a request: `onRequest`, `transform`, `beforeRoute`, `afterRoute`, `mapResponse`, `onError`. Put global hooks in `src/hooks.ts` and route hooks in the route's `hooks.ts`.
- **Plugins** add features to your app. Register them in `src/plugins.ts`.
- **Providers** register shared services in `src/providers.ts`. You read them from `ctx.services`.

See [Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/system) and [Ecosystem](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/introduction).

## OpenAPI

BurgerAPI builds an OpenAPI document from your routes and schemas. It serves the docs UI at `/docs`.

See [OpenAPI & Swagger](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/openapi).

## CLI and deployment

The CLI creates projects (`create`), adds hooks and plugins (`add`), runs the dev server (`dev`), and builds for production (`build`). Pick a platform with `--target`: `bun` (default), `node`, `cloudflare`, `deno`, or `vercel`.

WebSocket routes work on every target except Vercel.

See [CLI Tool](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/cli), [Deployment](https://burger-api.com/docs/deployment/bun), and [Compatibility](https://burger-api.com/docs/compatibility).

## Related

- [Quick Start](https://burger-api.com/docs/quick-start)
- [Installation](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/installation)
- [JavaScript](https://burger-api.com/docs/javascript)

# JavaScript

You can write a BurgerAPI app in JavaScript. Every convention file works with `.js` and `.mjs`, the same as `.ts`. You get type checking from JSDoc comments.

## Create a JavaScript project

```bash
burger-api create my-api --lang js
```

You get the same project with `.js` files. A `jsconfig.json` with `checkJs: true` makes your editor check your JSDoc types and give you autocomplete.

## Write a route

Use the same uppercase handler exports as TypeScript. Add types with JSDoc:

```js
// src/api/hello/route.js
/**
 * @param {import('burger-api').BurgerContext} ctx
 * @returns {Promise<Response>}
 */
export async function GET(ctx) {
  const name = ctx.query.name ?? "world";
  return Response.json({ message: `Hello, ${name}!` });
}
```

A route folder must not contain both `route.js` and `route.ts`. The app fails to start if it does.

## Validated data

Put the schema in `schema.js`. Use `@satisfies`, not `@type`, so `defineRoute` can infer the types of `ctx.validated`:

```js
// src/api/products/schema.js
import { z } from "zod";

/** @satisfies {import('burger-api').MethodSchema} */
export const POST = {
  body: z.object({ name: z.string() }),
};
```

```js
// src/api/products/route.js
import { defineRoute } from "burger-api";
import { POST as PostSchema } from "./schema";

export const POST = defineRoute(PostSchema, (ctx) => {
  const { name } = ctx.validated.body;
  return Response.json({ created: { name } }, { status: 201 });
});
```

## Common JSDoc types

- `@param {import('burger-api').BurgerContext} ctx` for handlers and hooks.
- `@type {import('burger-api').Hook}` for hook functions.
- `@type {import('burger-api').Plugin}` for plugins.
- `@type {import('burger-api').OpenAPIMeta}` for entries in `openapi.js`.

## Generate files

`burger-api generate` sees `jsconfig.json` and creates `.js` files:

```bash
burger-api generate route users
```

## Related

- [Key Concepts](https://burger-api.com/docs/key-concepts)
- [Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/system)

# Migrating from 0.9.x

This guide is for apps running `burger-api` `0.9.x` and `@burger-api/cli` `0.9.x`. The `0.9.x` line stays on npm (`burger-api@0.9.7`, `@burger-api/cli@0.9.9`), so the move is not urgent, but it is a rewrite rather than a patch. Three things changed at the core:

- Middleware became **hooks**: six named lifecycle points instead of a middleware chain.
- `BurgerRequest` became **`BurgerContext`**: one typed context for every hook and handler.
- Configuration moved into convention files: `src/hooks.ts`, `src/plugins.ts`, `burger.build.ts`.

Plan for an afternoon for a small API, longer if you have custom auth or global middleware. The [hook system](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/system), [validation](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/zod), and [configuration](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/configuration) pages explain the new model in full; this page is about getting your old code across.

## Upgrade the packages

```bash
bun add burger-api@latest
bun add -g @burger-api/cli@latest
```

Deploying to plain Node.js? Add the official adapter as well:

```bash
bun add @burger-api/node-server
```

## Checklist

| 0.9.x | 1.0.0-beta | What to do |
|-------|------------|------------|
| `BurgerRequest` | `BurgerContext` | Rename the import and the parameter. Handlers are `export async function GET(ctx: BurgerContext)`. See [Request Context](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/request-handling). |
| `Middleware` type and the middleware chain | Hooks (`onRequest`, `transform`, `beforeRoute`, `afterRoute`, `mapResponse`, `onError`) | Decide what each middleware was doing: stop, decorate, or transform. Map it to the matching hook. See [Hook System](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/system). |
| Route `export const middleware` in `route.ts` | Route `hooks.ts` | Move the code to a `hooks.ts` next to `route.ts`. `beforeRoute` replaces a middleware that short-circuits; `afterRoute` / `mapResponse` replace one that returns a response transform. |
| `globalMiddleware` in `new Burger({...})` | `src/hooks.ts` | Export global hooks from `src/hooks.ts` (`onRequest` for work before routing, `beforeRoute` for work after validation). |
| CLI `burger-api serve` | `burger-api dev` | Rename the command and any package script that calls it. |
| `burger.config.ts` | `burger.build.ts` | Rename the file. It is build-time only; `dev` and `start` read `new Burger({...})`. `doctor` flags the old name as an error. |
| `middleware.ts` / `use.ts` / `webhook.ts` route files | `config.ts`, `hooks.ts`, plugins | A leftover file is a startup error: `Forbidden convention file`. Delete it, then move the logic to hooks, plugins, or `config.ts`. |
| Auth factories in `ecosystem/middlewares/` (`jwt`, `apiKey`, ...) | Plugins in `ecosystem/plugins/` (`jwtAuth`, `apiKey`, ...) | Install with `burger-api add jwt-auth` and register in `src/plugins.ts`. See [Ecosystem](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/introduction). |
| Group/folder files shared across routes | Self-contained route directories | Groups only strip the URL. Copy shared `schema.ts` / `hooks.ts` code into each route that needs it, or import a shared module. See [File-Based Routing](https://burger-api.com/docs/routing/file-based-routing). |
| `req.validated?.query` with a manual generic | `ctx.validated.query` via `defineRoute` / `defineHooks` | Per-method `schema.ts` exports plus `defineRoute` infer `ctx.validated` with no generic to write. |
| Validation errors: `400` with `{ errors }` | `422` Problem Details (RFC 9457) | Update clients and tests. `errorFormat: "plain"` in validation config gets the old-style body shape back. See [Validation Errors](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/errors). |
| Body schema skipped non-JSON bodies | Body schema rejects non-JSON with `415` | Send `application/json` (or `application/*+json`), or drop the body schema for form endpoints. |
| `req.validated` optionally populated | `ctx.validated` always an object after validation | The slots you declared are typed non-optional; other slots are `unknown`. |
| `req.params` and `req.wildcardParams` optional | `ctx.params` object, `ctx.wildcardParams` array, both always present | Remove null checks; `{}` / `[]` are the empty values. |
| Mutable `ctx.services` per request | One frozen, shared `ctx.services` | Assigning keys now throws. Put per-request values in a `transform` hook instead. |
| `ctx.set` plain object | Tracked `ctx.set` | Keep using `ctx.set` for status and headers; it now tracks changes so untouched responses are returned as-is. |
| OpenAPI metadata `openapi` export in `route.ts`, title in `new Burger({...})` | `openapi.ts` per-method exports, document metadata in `src/openapi.config.ts` | Move metadata into its own file; `new Burger({ title })` still works as a fallback. See [OpenAPI](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/openapi). |
| A handler could return a non-`Response` | Non-`Response` returns fail loud with a 500 | Always return `Response.json(...)` or `new Response(...)`. |

## Step by step

### 1. A route handler

Before (`0.9.x`):

```ts title="api/products/route.ts"
import type { BurgerRequest } from "burger-api";

export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
    const query = new URL(req.url).searchParams;
    return Response.json({ search: query.get("search") });
}
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`):

```ts title="src/api/products/route.ts"
import type { BurgerContext } from "burger-api";

export async function GET(ctx: BurgerContext) {
    return Response.json({ search: ctx.query.search });
}
```

`ctx.query` is parsed lazily from the request, so you no longer build a `URL` by hand. See [Request Context](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/request-handling) for every property.

### 2. Route middleware becomes route hooks

Before (`0.9.x`), middleware in `route.ts` did three different jobs in one shape:

```ts title="api/products/route.ts"
import type { BurgerRequest, Middleware } from "burger-api";

export const middleware: Middleware[] = [
    (req: BurgerRequest) => {
        if (req.headers.get("x-admin") !== "true") {
            return Response.json({ error: "Forbidden" }, { status: 403 });
        }
        return async (response) => {
            response.headers.set("x-products", "1");
            return response;
        };
    },
];

export async function GET(req: BurgerRequest) {
    return Response.json({ items: [] });
}
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`), the auth check and the transform are separate hook points in `hooks.ts`:

```ts title="src/api/products/hooks.ts"
import { ForbiddenError } from "burger-api";
import type { RouteHooks } from "burger-api";

export const transform: RouteHooks["transform"] = {
    admin: (ctx) => {
        if (ctx.headers.get("x-admin") !== "true") {
            throw new ForbiddenError("Forbidden");
        }
        return true;
    },
};

export const afterRoute: RouteHooks["afterRoute"] = () => (response) => {
    response.headers.set("x-products", "1");
    return response;
};
```

Mapping rules:

- A middleware that checked credentials or roles becomes a `transform` entry that throws an `HTTPError`.
- A middleware that returned a `Response` to stop for another reason becomes a `beforeRoute` hook that returns a `Response`.
- A middleware that returned a function `(response) => response` becomes `afterRoute` or `mapResponse` returning that function. `mapResponse` is the last chance to change headers.
- A middleware that returned `undefined` becomes a hook that returns `undefined`.

`onRequest` is app-level only. You cannot scope it to one route: declaring it in a route's `hooks.ts` fails the TypeScript check, and the runtime warns and ignores it. See [Route Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/route-specific).

### 3. Global middleware becomes `src/hooks.ts`

Before (`0.9.x`):

```ts title="index.ts"
import { Burger } from "burger-api";
import { logger } from "./middleware/logger";

const burger = new Burger({
    apiDir: "./api",
    globalMiddleware: [logger],
});

burger.serve(4000);
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`), the entry stays small and the hooks live in a convention file:

```ts title="src/index.ts"
import { Burger } from "burger-api";

const burger = new Burger({
    apiDir: "./src/api",
});

burger.serve(4000);
```

```ts title="src/hooks.ts"
import { logger } from "../ecosystem/hooks/logger/logger";

export const onRequest = [logger()];
```

The same applies to CORS and rate limiting: install the hook from the ecosystem with `burger-api add cors` and compose it in `src/hooks.ts`. See [Global Hooks](https://burger-api.com/docs/hooks/global) and [Ecosystem](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/introduction).

### 4. Validation schema

Before (`0.9.x`), schema and handler were coupled in one file with lowercase method keys:

```ts title="api/products/route.ts"
import { z } from "zod";
import type { BurgerRequest } from "burger-api";

export const schema = {
    get: {
        query: z.object({ search: z.string() }),
    },
    post: {
        body: z.object({ name: z.string() }),
    },
};

export async function GET(
    req: BurgerRequest<{ query: z.infer<typeof schema.get.query> }>
) {
    return Response.json({ search: req.validated?.query });
}

export async function POST(
    req: BurgerRequest<{ body: z.infer<typeof schema.post.body> }>
) {
    return Response.json({ name: req.validated?.body?.name });
}
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`), the schema is its own file with uppercase per-method exports, and `defineRoute` infers the types:

```ts title="src/api/products/schema.ts"
import { z } from "zod";

export const GET = { query: z.object({ search: z.string() }) };
export const POST = { body: z.object({ name: z.string() }) };
```

```ts title="src/api/products/route.ts"
import { defineRoute } from "burger-api";
import { GET as GetSchema, POST as PostSchema } from "./schema";

export const GET = defineRoute(GetSchema, (ctx) => {
    const { search } = ctx.validated.query;
    return Response.json({ search });
});

export const POST = defineRoute(PostSchema, (ctx) => {
    const { name } = ctx.validated.body;
    return Response.json({ name });
});
```

Two behavior changes to watch for:

- A failed validation is now a `422` Problem Details response, not a `400` with `{ errors }`. See [Validation Errors](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/errors).
- When a body schema is declared, a non-JSON body (`text/plain`, form data) is rejected with `415 Unsupported Media Type` instead of skipping validation.

The old manual generic (`BurgerContext<typeof RouteSchema>`) still works when you prefer it. See [Schema Definition](https://burger-api.com/docs/validation/schema).

### 5. Auth middleware becomes a plugin

Before (`0.9.x`), auth was middleware added to `globalMiddleware`:

```ts title="index.ts"
import { Burger } from "burger-api";
import { jwt } from "./ecosystem/middlewares/jwt-auth/jwt-auth";

const burger = new Burger({
    apiDir: "./api",
    globalMiddleware: [jwt({ secret: process.env.JWT_SECRET! })],
});

burger.serve(4000);
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`), auth is a plugin registered in `src/plugins.ts`, and routes opt in or out in `config.ts`:

```ts title="src/plugins.ts"
import type { PluginRegistrar } from "burger-api";
import { jwtAuth } from "../ecosystem/plugins/jwt-auth/jwt-auth";

export default (burger: PluginRegistrar) => {
    burger.usePlugin(jwtAuth({ secret: process.env.JWT_SECRET }));
};
```

```ts title="src/api/public/health/config.ts"
export default { auth: false };
```

```ts title="src/api/admin/config.ts"
export default { auth: { required: true, roles: ["admin"] } };
```

The plugin attaches the decoded token as `ctx.user`. API keys work the same way with `apiKey({ keys: [...] })`. See [JWT Auth](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/jwt-auth) and [API Key Auth](https://burger-api.com/docs/ecosystem/api-key-auth).

### 6. Build config

Before (`0.9.x`):

```ts title="burger.config.ts"
export default {
    apiDir: "./api",
    pageDir: "./pages",
    apiPrefix: "/api",
    pagePrefix: "/",
    debug: false,
};
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`):

```ts title="burger.build.ts"
import type { BuildConfig } from "burger-api";

export default {
    apiDir: "./src/api",
    pageDir: "./src/pages",
    apiPrefix: "/api",
    pagePrefix: "/",
    debug: false,
} satisfies Partial<BuildConfig>;
```

`burger.build.ts` is read by `burger-api build`, `inspect`, and `doctor` only. Runtime options live in `new Burger({...})`, and `doctor` warns when the two disagree. See [Configuration](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/configuration).

### 7. CLI commands in package.json

Before (`0.9.x`), scripts called Bun directly:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "bun --watch src/index.ts",
    "start": "bun src/index.ts",
    "build": "bun build src/index.ts --outdir ./dist"
  }
}
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`), scripts call the CLI, which the project should carry as a dependency:

```json title="package.json"
{
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "burger-api dev",
    "start": "burger-api start",
    "build": "burger-api build src/index.ts",
    "typecheck": "bun check"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@burger-api/cli": "^1.0.0-beta"
  }
}
```

Add `--target=<platform>` when you build for something other than Bun: `burger-api build src/index.ts --target=node`. See [CLI Tool](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/cli) and [Build Command](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/build).

### 8. OpenAPI metadata

Before (`0.9.x`), metadata was an `openapi` export in `route.ts` and a title in the constructor:

```ts title="api/products/route.ts"
export const openapi = {
    get: {
        summary: "List products",
        tags: ["Products"],
    },
};
```

```ts title="index.ts"
const burger = new Burger({
    apiDir: "./api",
    title: "My API",
    description: "Products and orders",
});
```

After (`1.0.0-beta`), route metadata moves to `openapi.ts` with per-method exports, and document metadata moves to `src/openapi.config.ts`:

```ts title="src/api/products/openapi.ts"
export const GET = {
    summary: "List products",
    tags: ["Products"],
};
```

```ts title="src/openapi.config.ts"
import type { OpenAPIConfig } from "burger-api";

export default {
    title: "My API",
    description: "Products and orders",
    version: "1.0.0",
} satisfies OpenAPIConfig;
```

The spec is served at `/openapi.json` and the docs UI at `/docs`, as before. Swagger UI is still the default; `scalarDocs()` and `redocDocs()` are also built in. See [OpenAPI](https://burger-api.com/docs/api/openapi).

## Verify the upgrade

Run these from the project root:

```bash
burger-api doctor
burger-api inspect
bun run dev
bun run typecheck
bun test
```

- `doctor` checks the project shape and fails on leftover `burger.config.ts`. See [Doctor](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/doctor).
- `inspect` lists the config, routes, hooks, and plugins the CLI actually discovers, which catches files the scanner is not loading. See [Inspect](https://burger-api.com/docs/cli/inspect).
- `bun run dev` starts the server with hot reload. Open `/docs` to confirm the spec still generates.

## Getting help

If something here does not work, or the migration guide is missing a case, [open an issue](https://github.com/isfhan/burger-api/issues). The `0.9.7` release stays on npm while you work through the upgrade.

- [Request Context](https://burger-api.com/docs/core/request-handling)

- [CLI Tool](https://burger-api.com/docs/getting-started/cli)
